added_failures_note: measured by the reviewer: the reviewed run's manifest names no baseline_suite or after_suite, so the count comes from arms I ran at the pinned revisions. Base 02a98eb0e on tests/cli/test_discover_signals_stage.py + tests/discovery/{test_signals_pipeline,test_parallel,test_signal_checking,test_signal_check_carry_forward,test_singleton_sources}.py: 150 passed EXIT=0 (logs/base_arm.log). Head 760ab572b on the same selection: 2 failed, 148 passed EXIT=1 (logs/head_arm.log). Both added ids are stale tests asserting the refusal the change removed.
call_sites: build_focus_predicate is called only from imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py (the two claim queries and the pending-work probes); resolve_focus_items is the shared resolver in imas_codex/cli/discover/common.py already used by the candidate stage, and run_signals_stage is its one production caller. No other production caller.

findings.text: follow-on (the added failures this diff introduces): test_focus_items_are_refused_stating_the_mechanism and test_cli_focus_is_refused still assert the removed refusal message ('claim query takes no item filter'). Both pass at the pinned base and fail at the pinned head -- base arm 150 passed EXIT=0, head arm 2 failed 148 passed EXIT=1 (logs/base_arm.log, logs/head_arm.log). At head the stage now reaches _validate_focus and raises click.UsageError("--focus names unknown signal or source id(s) at jet: MAG/coil"), which is the intended new behaviour, so the two tests encode behaviour the change deliberately removed and must be rewritten (focus reaches the engine; an unknown focus id is a usage error naming itself). The file is outside the reviewed node's write scope and the reviewed manifest already records it as a follow-on.

follow-on (latent, not observed): _validate_focus accepts a focus item that matches any node's own data_source_path array segment, while build_focus_predicate resolves an array segment only through a member's path inside a MEMBER_OF source. A FacilitySignal that carries the segment but belongs to no SignalSource would therefore pass validation and then select nothing -- a silent no-op of exactly the kind the validator exists to prevent. I probed the live graph and found 0 source-less jt-60sa signals whose path carries magPbTC10, and SignalSource carries no data_source_path property (keys: facility_id, group_key, id, keywords, members_described, member_count, physics_domain, representative_id, status), so the two query shapes agree on every node the graph currently holds; the mismatch is a code shape that a future source-less signal would reach, not a present defect.

follow-on: the claim tests drive a MagicMock _Catalogue whose _named_sources reimplements the focus resolution itself and whose query() asserts the claim Cypher contains the idiom substrings ('s.id IN $focus_items', '(s)-[:MEMBER_OF]->(source:SignalSource)', 'split(coalesce(named.data_source_path, ...')) before applying its own Python selection; a rewrite of build_focus_predicate that kept those substrings but changed the Cypher semantics would leave every claim assertion green, so the query itself is verified by the live graph check, not by the gate.

item_verdicts.call_sites: build_focus_predicate is called only from imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py (the two claim queries and the pending-work probes); resolve_focus_items is the shared resolver in imas_codex/cli/discover/common.py already used by the candidate stage, and run_signals_stage is its one production caller. No other production caller.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 02a98eb0e. 89389b7ea adds build_focus_predicate (selects a signal by its own id or accessor, or by any SignalSource it is MEMBER_OF whose id is named or any of whose members carries a named data_source_path array segment), renders it into the enrichment channel-skip and claim queries, the check claim, and the two pending-work probes, threads focus_items through them, and replaces the CLI refusal with resolve_focus_items plus _validate_focus. 760ab572b extends _validate_focus and the predicate's docstring so a focus item may also name a source through a member handle (signal id, accessor, or array segment), and adds tests for the array-to-group resolution while keeping the unnamed-source negative control.
item_verdicts.done_when: section 1's measure is four things. (1) '--focus magPbTC10 claims only the signals whose SignalSource is named': verified live, the predicate selects 28 signals across exactly the two named sources out of the facility's discovered population. (2) 'a unit test proves an unnamed source in the same facility is left unclaimed': tests/discovery/test_signals_focus.py::test_unnamed_source_in_the_same_facility_stays_unclaimed runs for both claim queries and is the raw target of the negative control below. (3) 'an unknown focus identity fails with a usage error that names it': _validate_focus raises click.UsageError('--focus names unknown signal or source id(s) at <facility>: <item>'), asserted by test_validate_focus_names_the_unknown_item and test_stage_refuses_an_unknown_focus_item, and observed live as the head-arm failure of the stale test. (4) 'the focused signals tests pass, run with -n 8': the new file is 13 passed EXIT=0 (the run's own head_gate.log with -n 8) and my serial re-run at the pinned head is 13 passed EXIT=0 (logs/head_focus_gate.log). All four are met at the pinned head.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that a system cohort can enrich only its own signal sources. The diff adds build_focus_predicate and threads focus_items through both claim queries, the two pending-work probes, both workers and the engine entry point, and replaces the CLI refusal with resolve_focus_items plus _validate_focus. A live read against the jt-60sa graph confirms the rendered predicate --focus magPbTC10 selects exactly the members of the two named sources (28 signals = 14 MDAC + 14 PSRC), the full MDAC magPbTCNNN source id selects its 14 members, and the singleton member id selects 1, so the goal is met.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records status complete, commits 89389b7ea and 760ab572b, a 13-passed focused gate and a 137-passed adjacent gate, a negative_control.log whose FAILED ids match its note, and it names the two stale tests under follow_ons. It carries no baseline_suite or after_suite block, so the added-failure figures below come from the base and head arms I ran myself.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git diff --name-status 02a98eb0e..760ab572b lists exactly four paths: docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-mapping-study-expansion/signals-focus.html (added), imas_codex/cli/discover/signals.py (modified), imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py (modified), tests/discovery/test_signals_focus.py (added) -- exactly the manifest's declared write paths, with no generated model and nothing outside the fence.

justifications.durability: the guard fires: my reproduction of the reviewed run's mutation reddens test_unnamed_source_in_the_same_facility_stays_unclaimed for both claim queries, so the unnamed source is admitted only when the filter is dropped. Durability is docked because the claim tests assert the query's idiom substrings through a mock that reimplements the resolution in Python, so the gate alone would not catch a semantic change that preserved the substrings; the live-graph read is what currently carries that assurance.
justifications.evidence: the reviewed run's own gate logs record 13 passed and 137 passed, and I re-ran the pinned arms myself: base 02a98eb0e 150 passed EXIT=0 and head 760ab572b 2 failed 148 passed EXIT=1 on the same six pre-existing files, and head 13 passed EXIT=0 on the new file (logs/base_arm.log, logs/head_arm.log, logs/head_focus_gate.log). I reproduced the negative control independently (mutation: force build_focus_predicate to return empty): 7 failed 6 passed EXIT=1 (logs/negative_control_repro.log), and I verified the live claim on the graph myself (magPbTC10 -> 28 = 14+14; MDAC source id -> 14; singleton id -> 1).
justifications.fit: the change follows the module's shape -- a single predicate helper beside build_category_predicate, the claim functions gain a focus_items parameter exactly as they carry categories and scanner_types, and the CLI resolves focus the way the candidate stage already does -- so it sits with the surrounding code rather than beside it.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the deliverable is met: focus reaches every claim path and the CLI, and a live read confirms the named source's members are selected and nothing else. The one reservation is that the change leaves two existing tests asserting the behaviour it removed, so the repository as merged is red on tests/cli/test_discover_signals_stage.py until the follow-on lands.
justifications.reuse: the diff reuses resolve_focus_items rather than minting a second manifest parser (as section 1 requires) and extends claim_signals_for_enrichment/check in place; the only duplication is that _validate_focus re-expresses the predicate's resolution rule (id, accessor, data_source_path segment) in a second query that re-derives it.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff touches exactly the four declared paths and nothing else -- no generated model, no file outside the fence.
